final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor reframed the same record and expressly conceded that the key predicate remains unproven. The admissible evidence still shows: aggregate readiness passed and there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents; a current subgroup regression exists for a named launch use case; and policy permits certification only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material weakness is disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. That missing documentation/mitigation predicate is not a minor caveat layered onto an otherwise complete compliance showing. It is the compliance condition itself. For that reason, the record supports at most a potentially supportable future certification after the disclosure or approved-mitigation condition is evidenced, not compliant_with_caveats on the present record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation or model card was updated before certification to disclose the developer-support migration weakness.
No admissible evidence shows approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance covering the current subgroup regression.
The actor's caveated theory depends on a disclosure predicate that remains unproven on the current record.
Prior approval and informal post-launch monitoring remain contextual only and cannot satisfy the current-policy requirement.
